doc.title: Dianne Reeves interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, October 13, 2001

title: Audio excerpt of a country preacher song and George Duke with Cannonball
summary: She explains writing lyrics to a piece about a country preacher, then recalls seeing George Duke with Cannonball Adderley, who educated his audiences.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Cannonball Adderley: the sound, the man, the band

blocks.x: That’s good. I have one more little piece of music that I’d like to play for you. It’s been a favorite of mine and I think it was a favorite of yours.
I was impressed by what you were playing between your breaks too. What led you to this?

Well see it’s about a country preacher and when you listen to the way that he is playing, and when you listen to the song, you feel all of those things. And that’s why I wrote the lyrics to this, because I love this.
I wish I had been there for that moment. It’s just unbelievable.
Interesting that George Duke ended up with Cannonball too.
Actually I saw him with Cannon.

Yeah. It was like wow, this is incredible. The other thing I liked is when he was on stage he really let the audience know what they were going to do, what the music was about, so you felt you had an education. You were waiting for certain thing to happen because he said that this is what this song is about and this is, you know, he kind of educated his audience, which I loved.
